official_sources: Planning Listed Buildings Conservation Areas Act 1990

official_measurement_examples.name: Current collection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reported 11,007 conservation-area records; collector last ran and new data was found on 24 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Coverage limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data states the conservation-area dataset is incomplete and contains duplicate areas still being reconciled.

official_measurement_examples.name: Demolition control
official_measurement_examples.fact: Relevant demolition of certain unlisted buildings in conservation areas can require planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Article 4 separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Conservation-area designation and an Article 4 direction are distinct controls and must not be collapsed into one status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Tree notice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Work to qualifying trees in a conservation area can require six weeks notice under section 211; this is distinct from TPO consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Not blanket prohibition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Conservation-area designation is a heritage planning consideration, not a blanket prohibition on development.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local appraisal context
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current local conservation-area appraisals and management documents matter for character and appearance assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Conservation-area boundaries do not establish title, access rights or final development yield.

core_rules: conservation-area dataset is incomplete and may contain duplicates
conservation area is not Article 4 direction
conservation-area status is not automatic refusal
relevant demolition can require planning permission
planning permission for demolition is proposal specific
tree section 211 notice is distinct from TPO consent
six-week notice is not blanket tree-work permission
current local appraisal and boundary version must be retained
conservation-area document is not itself planning permission
designation does not calculate development yield
permitted-development restrictions depend on current rules and local directions
absence from Planning Data is not proof of no conservation area
historic and current boundaries must remain distinct
no parcel conservation-area clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Planning Data, Historic England, GOV.UK, legislation and current local-authority sources checked on 2026-07-26. July 2026 coverage limits, demolition, Article 4 and section 211 distinctions retained; no parcel promotion.
